creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Eight or more scripts hand-assemble query strings: `catalog-hosts.rad:16-24`, `mm-channel-posts:72-77`, `rd:27-35`, `promq:76-81,109`, `rdmap:17`.

Spaces already encode - `sanitizeUrlString` (`core/requester.go:281`) has handled them since v0.6.13, and two of the review's own reports got this wrong before being corrected. The real corruption case is a literal `&`, `=`, or `?` inside a value, which nothing currently escapes.

---

### Orientation
- Same single shared closure as the other http cards: `createHttpFunctions()` at `core/funcs.go:1890-1966`. `query=` is read once and applies to all nine methods.
- URL normalization happens downstream of the builtin, in `sanitizeUrlString` (`core/requester.go:281`, confirmed at that exact line), called from `Requester.Request` at `core/requester.go:163`.
- Signatures come from `docs/funcs/http_*.md`, not Go. The `## Signature` line IS the type checker's signature.

### Where to start
- `core/funcs.go:164-181` - add `namedArgQuery` to the `namedArg*` const block.
- `core/funcs.go:1912-1962` - the `Execute` body. `url` is read at :1912; the query map is read and appended around there, before `NewRequestDef` at :1958.
- All nine `docs/funcs/http_*.md`: add the parameter to `## Signature` and to the `## Notes` table.
- Worth reading first: `safeQueryEscape` (`core/requester.go:271-275`) is the existing encoder - `url.QueryEscape` with `+` normalized to `%20`. Encoding a `query=` map should produce output that survives `sanitizeUrlString` unchanged.

### Premise refinement (verified)
Spaces do already encode, as the card says. Of the three characters the card lists, only `&` actually corrupts:

- `?q=a%26b&z=1` round-trips intact - `PathUnescape` then `safeQueryEscape` is idempotent (verified against `bin/radd` with `--mock-response`).
- A literal `=` inside a value survives: `SplitN(p, "=", 2)` at `core/requester.go:297` keeps the remainder as the value and re-escapes it to `%3D`.
- A literal `?` inside a value survives: `url.Parse` puts everything after the first `?` into `RawQuery`, and it re-escapes to `%3F`.
- A literal `&` does not survive: `core/requester.go:289` splits `RawQuery` on `&`, so `?q=a&b` becomes two parameters. By the time the hand-assembled string reaches `sanitizeUrlString` the ambiguity is unrecoverable - which is exactly the argument for `query=`.

### How to verify
```sh
make build
go test ./core/testing/ -run TestSnapshots -update=functions/http
go test ./core/testing/
make generate && make verify-generated
```
Snapshot suite is `core/testing/snapshots/functions/`. The sanitized URL that actually went out is captured (`core/requester.go:190`) and asserted by `assertHttpInvocationUrls` (`core/testing/test_helpers.go:568`); the mock line printed to stderr also shows it, which is what snapshot `### STDERR ###` blocks pick up.

### Done when
- A value containing `&`, `=`, `?`, `#`, `/` or a space passed via `query=` arrives correctly percent-encoded.
- Behavior when both a literal `?...` in the url and a `query=` map are given is decided and documented (append vs. reject).
- All nine doc files updated and `make verify-generated` clean.
- Snapshot cases under `core/testing/snapshots/functions/` covering at minimum the `&`-in-value case that motivates the card.

### Watch out for
- Everything goes through the `RReq` seam (`core/global.go:44`); `core/testing/` injects a Requester with mocked responses (`core/testing/test_helpers.go:135-156`). No direct `net/http`.
- `sanitizeUrlString` runs on whatever URL you build, so double-encoding is the risk: it decodes with `PathUnescape` before re-encoding, meaning a `%26` you emit survives, but a `%2526` does not mean what you think. Build the query as plain text and let one encoder own it.
- Parameter order is deliberately preserved in `sanitizeUrlString` (`core/requester.go:288`, comment explains `url.ParseQuery` loses it). A `query=` map is unordered - decide and document the ordering (Rad maps preserve insertion order, so following that is the least surprising choice).
title: http: accept a query= params map
